# Agents on Radar

> A live, sourced feed of real things people hand to AI agents (inbox and phone calls, shopping, travel, family, health, work, small business), with real popularity numbers, plain-English guides, copy-paste prompts, build-your-own-bot blueprints and tips to run your bots for less.

Data as of 2026-10-21. Popularity numbers are real counts (X likes/reposts, Reddit upvotes) with the date measured; unknown values are omitted.

## Start here
- [What can bots actually do?](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/what-can-bots-do/): plain-English explainer
- [AI agent examples for everyday life](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/ai-agent-examples/): every example on one page, grouped by part of life
- [Trending now](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/trending/)
- [Bot blueprints](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/): build-your-own-bot recipes
- [Latest in AI](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/news/): new models, agent launches and AI price changes in plain words, with sources (RSS: https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/news/feed.xml)
- [Run your bots for less](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/run-your-bots-for-less/): how to reduce AI API costs (model choice, free tiers, caching, batch, schedules, spend limits)
- [AI agent cost calculator](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/run-your-bots-for-less/#calculator): pick a bot or enter runs and message size, compare monthly cost across 18 models from official prices checked 2026-10-21; prefill with ?bot=<blueprint-slug>
- [AI price table](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/ai-pricing/): official API and plan prices for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Groq, Mistral, Meta and DeepSeek, checked 2026-10-21
- [RSS feed of new use cases](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/feed.xml)

## Use cases by category

### Inbox, calls & paperwork
- [Send a long video or thread to your bot with one reply](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/send-a-long-video-or-thread-to-your-bot/): See a long video or X thread you don't have time for? Reply to it by tagging your bot, and a short summary waits for you in your bot's app later.
- [Send all your newsletters to your bot and get one daily report](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/newsletter-daily-report/): Subscribe your newsletters to your bot's own email address. It reads every issue and sends you one short report each day, with a score that tells you which ones are worth reading in full.
- [Have your bot make a customer-service phone call for you](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/make-a-customer-service-call/): Some jobs still need a phone call, like cancelling a service or sorting out an account. With a phone-calling add-on, your bot can make the call, sit on hold and report back.
- [Hand your most-hated weekly chores to a personal agent](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/hand-your-most-hated-chores-to-a-personal-agent/): Personal agents like Meta Muse, Grok Bot and Gemini Spark work in the background on a schedule. Start with the chore you hate most.
- [Get a daily scam check on your inbox](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/email-scam-filter/): A read-only bot reads your new email each morning and gives each suspicious message a risk score and the red flags.
- [Have a bot sort your scanned paper mail and flag what needs you](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/sort-scanned-paper-mail-with-alerts/): A virtual mailbox service scans your paper mail to email. The bot reads every letter, queues up the routine ones for your OK, and pulls you in only when something looks unusual.
- [Give your agent its own email address](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/give-your-agent-its-own-email-address/): Give your agent an inbox of its own. Then you or anyone else can forward it jobs, like a meeting request it turns into a calendar invite with prep notes.
- [Get a Monday recap of your inbox and a to-do list](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/monday-inbox-recap-and-todo/): Every Monday a bot reviews last week's email, recaps what matters and suggests a ranked to-do list.
- [Only see the emails that actually need a reply](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/flag-only-emails-that-need-a-reply/): A simple triage bot flags anything needing a reply within 24 hours and moves the noise out of the way.
- [Get a 2-minute morning digest on topics you care about](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/morning-news-digest/): A bot reads the news on your topics every morning and sends you a short plain-English digest, or even an audio version.
- [Watch your email for one important letter or reply](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/watch-for-one-important-letter/): Waiting on a visa decision, a parcel or a reply from the landlord? Have a bot watch for it and ping you.
- [Understand a confusing letter or notice (and know what to do next)](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/understand-a-confusing-letter/): A letter from a government office, insurer, bank or landlord landed in your mailbox and you can't tell if it's important, a bill, a scam, or nothing.
- [Write a complaint that actually gets a problem fixed](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/write-a-complaint-that-gets-fixed/): A company messed up (late delivery, broken product, wrong charge, bad repair) and customer service keeps going in circles.
- [Get through a long form without the headache](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/fill-out-a-long-form/): A long application or government form is confusing, and you're not sure what each question is really asking.
- [Review a rental lease before you sign](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/review-a-lease-before-signing/): The lease is long, the landlord wants it signed this week, and you're worried about what's buried in it.
- [Make a moving checklist and change your address everywhere](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/moving-checklist-and-change-of-address/): Moving means telling dozens of companies and offices your new address, and something always gets missed.
- [Get your email inbox under control](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/clean-up-your-email-inbox/): Thousands of unread emails, and the important ones get buried under newsletters and promos.

### Run your bots for less
- [Set spend limits and usage alerts on your AI accounts](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/set-ai-spend-limits-and-alerts/): Before a bot runs on autopilot, put a hard cap on what it can spend and check usage weekly, so a runaway loop can't run up a big bill.
- [Keep your bot's prompts, tools and context short](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/keep-prompts-and-context-short/): You pay for everything the model reads on every run: your instructions, tool definitions, pasted pages and the conversation so far. Trimming those is often the easiest saving.
- [Stop always-on bots from burning tokens: run them less often, or on demand](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/schedule-bots-without-burning-tokens/): Every scheduled run costs tokens, even when nothing has changed. Match the schedule to how often the thing really changes, and switch fun-but-idle bots to run only when you ask.
- [Run open models on your own computer (or a cheap host) for simple jobs](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/run-open-models-on-your-own-computer/): Open-weight models can run on your own computer with a free tool like Ollama, so routine jobs cost nothing per message. Some hosts also run open models for a fraction of big-model prices.
- [Cut your AI bill with prompt caching and batch discounts](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/cut-costs-with-caching-and-batch/): If your bot sends the same long instructions every time, caching makes the repeat part much cheaper. If results can wait a few hours, batch processing halves the price at several providers.
- [Decide between a monthly AI plan and paying per use](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/subscription-or-pay-per-use/): A monthly plan (like Claude Pro) gives you a flat price with usage limits. Paying per use through an API costs exactly what you use. Which is cheaper depends on how much your bots run.
- [Build and test your bot on a free tier before you pay](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/test-your-bot-on-a-free-tier/): Several AI providers let you try their API or app for free. Use that to prove your bot works before you put a card on file, and know what you give up on the free tier.
- [Use a small model for simple jobs and save the big one for hard ones](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/pick-a-smaller-model-for-simple-jobs/): Most bot jobs (sorting email, summarizing, checking a page) don't need the most powerful model. The small models cost a fraction as much, so route easy work to them and only send hard problems up.

### Shopping & groceries
- [Have an agent research a used car from its listing link](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/research-a-used-car-from-a-listing/): Drop in a used-car listing link and let an agent dig in: what the model is known for, the car's damage history and the questions to ask before you call the seller.
- [Plan a week of family meals and fill the grocery cart](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/family-meal-plan-and-grocery-order/): A bot keeps your recipe list, writes the week's meal plan and turns it into a shopping list that fills your grocery cart.
- [Let an agent reorder your regular groceries](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/reorder-your-regular-groceries/): Some people now let an agent handle their weekly grocery order and switch stores when a better offer appears.
- [Have a bot watch any web page and ping you when it changes](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/watch-a-web-page-for-changes/): Instead of refreshing a page, tell a bot what matters on it. It checks on a schedule and pings you only when that changes.
- [Keep a household essentials list and reorder on time](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/household-restock-list/): A bot keeps a running list of essentials, asks once a week what's low and builds the reorder.
- [Give your agent a single-use card before it books or buys anything](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/pay-with-a-single-use-virtual-card/): When an agent books or buys for you, give it a one-time virtual card so it can't be charged again.

### Bookings & travel
- [Get roadside help abroad when nobody speaks your language](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/get-roadside-help-abroad/): Broken down in another country and the insurer's phone line is in a language you don't speak? An agent can find the right help form, fill it in with your details and get help moving.
- [Give your bot a phone number so it can call and book for you](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/call-and-book-by-phone/): Plenty of places still only take bookings by phone. Once your bot has its own number, it can call a restaurant, a vet or a salon, book the slot and tell you what was said.
- [Plan and book a whole trip by texting your bot](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/plan-and-book-a-whole-trip-by-text/): One parent says his bot booked the flight, the rental car, the vacation rental, a restaurant and event tickets, all over text.
- [Get rebooked fast when your flight is delayed](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/rebook-a-delayed-flight/): When a flight slips, an agent can find the fastest alternative that still gets you there on time and book it for you.
- [Get alerted the moment your airline changes your flight](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/catch-airline-schedule-changes/): Airlines quietly move flight times. An agent watching your inbox spots the change, tells you what moved, and lays out your options.
- [Book restaurant tables by message, even at phone-only places](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/restaurant-reservations-by-agent/): Restaurant bookings are the gateway task for many agent users, including small places that only take WhatsApp or calls.
- [Book a haircut or appointment, even when the form won't work](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/book-a-haircut-by-email/): When the online booking needs a local phone number, an agent can just email the business instead.
- [Have an AI agent find and book an appointment for you](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/book-an-appointment-with-an-ai-agent/): You need a DMV slot, a restaurant table or a service appointment, and you don't have time to click through booking sites or keep checking for openings.
- [Plan a trip itinerary that fits your pace](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/plan-a-trip-itinerary/): Planning a trip means 30 open tabs, and you still aren't sure the days fit together.

### Family & home
- [Have an agent contact tradespeople and line up quotes for a home project](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/line-up-contractors-for-a-home-project/): Instead of calling round electricians, plumbers and roofers yourself, let an agent reach out to all of them, collect their replies and put them side by side.
- [Get your phone number off people-search sites to cut spam calls](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/remove-your-number-from-people-search-sites/): A bot finds where your phone number is listed on people-search and data-broker sites, files the opt-out requests, and checks again later.
- [Catch family calendar clashes before the week starts](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/sunday-family-calendar-check/): Every Sunday a bot reads the next two weeks of your family calendar and school notices and flags the clashes.
- [Run family logistics from the family group chat](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/run-family-logistics-from-the-group-chat/): New “family agents” sit in your family chat and handle the small jobs: restocking, booking the dentist and reminders.
- [Turn the flood of school emails into one weekly digest](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/school-email-digest/): Label school emails and let an agent read them weekly. It pulls out deadlines, forms, payments and events, without duplicates.
- [Get 5 weekend activity ideas that fit your kids and the weather](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/weekend-family-activities/): Every Friday, get activity ideas matched to your kids' ages, the weather and your budget, with a rainy-day backup.
- [Make a weekly meal plan and grocery list in 5 minutes](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/weekly-meal-plan-and-grocery-list/): Deciding what's for dinner every night is exhausting, and you keep buying food that goes to waste.
- [Use AI for homework help that teaches instead of cheats](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/homework-help-that-teaches/): Your kid is stuck on homework, you don't remember how to do it, and you don't want the AI to just hand over answers.

### Health & care
- [Get pinged when a prescription is ready, and told when to leave](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/prescription-ready-and-time-to-leave/): A personal agent can sweep your email every morning for "ready for pickup" notices, and check live traffic before your appointments to tell you when to head out.
- [Log your meals by talking and get a daily weight check-in](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/log-meals-and-weight-by-voice/): Tell your bot what you ate, out loud, and it keeps the food log for you. It can also check in on your weight each morning.
- [Set up medication and appointment reminders for a parent](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/medication-reminders-for-a-parent/): Family agents can remind an older parent about medication and book routine appointments, with the family kept in the loop.
- [Appeal a health insurance denial with AI](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/appeal-a-health-insurance-denial/): Your health insurance said no to a treatment, test or medicine, and the letter is full of codes and jargon.
- [Prepare for a doctor's appointment in 10 minutes](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/prepare-for-a-doctor-visit/): Appointments are short, and you forget half your questions or can't explain your symptoms clearly.
- [Organize an aging parent's care and paperwork](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/organize-a-parents-care-paperwork/): You're helping a parent with doctors, insurance, medicines and bills, and the details live in a dozen places.

### Work & career
- [Give your agents their own Apple account so they share reminders, notes and calendar](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/give-your-agents-a-shared-apple-account/): A Mac signed in to a separate Apple Account can become the shared desk where your agents leave each other reminders, notes, calendar events and messages, while your personal account stays private.
- [Hand off tasks to your agent by voice while you drive](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/hand-off-tasks-by-voice-while-driving/): Long drive? Talk to your agent on a voice call and hand off research, follow-ups and to-dos, then find them done when you arrive.
- [Hand a clunky web form or app to an agent that uses the computer for you](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/hand-a-clunky-web-form-to-an-agent/): Some software you only touch once a year. A computer-use agent can click through it for you, from a login you control, while you watch.
- [Write a letter of recommendation for someone](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/write-a-letter-of-recommendation/): Someone asked you for a reference letter and you want it to sound specific and honest, not generic. AI can turn your notes and their resume into a solid first draft.
- [Write a resignation letter that keeps the door open](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/write-a-resignation-letter/): You're leaving a job and want to say so clearly and kindly, without oversharing. AI can draft a short, professional resignation letter or email in a couple of minutes.
- [Set up a “chief of staff” bot that plans your other bots](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/hire-a-chief-of-staff-bot/): Instead of building lots of bots, start with one that asks what you do and suggests which helpers you need.
- [Catch offers and deadlines the moment they land in your inbox](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/time-sensitive-inbox-watcher/): For fast-moving work (real estate, sales, hiring), a bot in your inbox and calendar texts you when something time-sensitive arrives.
- [Find the conversations you forgot to follow up on](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/find-dead-conversations-to-follow-up/): A weekly automation reads your calendar, inbox and tasks and lists people still waiting to hear back, with drafted nudges.
- [Get a daily digest of jobs that actually fit you](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/job-match-digest/): A scheduled workflow pulls new listings, scores them against your CV and emails you the best matches with draft notes. You still apply.
- [Teach a bot to write emails that sound like you](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/email-ghostwriter-style-guide/): Have the bot read your last 50 sent emails, write a style guide, then use it for every draft.
- [Tailor your resume and cover letter to a job in 15 minutes](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/tailor-your-resume-to-a-job/): Every job wants a slightly different resume, and rewriting yours each time takes forever.

### Small business & side hustles
- [Let your bot handle your website's contact email](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/let-your-bot-handle-your-sites-contact-email/): Forward the contact address of your website, club or class to your bot's own email. It reads each message, sums it up for you, and only answers when you say so.
- [Put a small team of agents on one project, each with its own job](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/team-of-agents-with-roles/): Instead of one chatbot doing everything, give separate agents separate roles (one researches, one builds) and let them hand work to each other in a shared conversation you can watch.
- [Match every business expense to its receipt, weekly](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/small-business-receipt-matching/): A read-only bot checks your card and payment activity against the receipts in a dedicated inbox and lists what's missing.
- [Run several brands or jobs with one bot each](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/one-bot-per-brand/): If you juggle several brands or clients, give each its own bot with its own tools, plus a coordinator that collects a daily note.
- [Build a list of local leads and approve every email](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/build-a-lead-list-with-approval/): A workflow finds businesses in your niche and area, researches each one and drafts a personal email. Nothing goes out until you approve it.
- [Log every new client inquiry automatically](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/log-new-client-inquiries/): When an inquiry email arrives, the bot pulls out the client's name and requested date, logs it in your tracker and sets up a folder.
- [Sell on Marketplace with an agent, with safety rules set first](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/sell-on-marketplace-with-rules/): Agents can answer buyers and schedule pickups, but set rules first. One story tells of an agent sharing an address and booking a pickup when the seller was out.
- [Get your ads and sales numbers every morning without logging in](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/daily-ads-and-sales-report/): A bot logs into your ad and sales dashboards (read-only) and sends a morning summary with what changed.
- [Write listings that sell your stuff faster](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/sell-your-stuff-online/): You have things to sell, but writing listings, pricing them and answering buyers is a chore.
- [Test a side hustle idea before you commit](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/test-a-side-hustle-idea/): You have an idea to earn extra money, but you don't know if anyone will pay, and ads promise 'easy AI income'.
- [Reply to customer reviews (even the angry ones)](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/reply-to-customer-reviews/): Reviews pile up on Google and you don't have time to answer, or a harsh review has you stuck on what to say.
- [Chase an unpaid invoice without burning the relationship](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/use-cases/chase-an-unpaid-invoice/): A client is late paying and you're not sure how firm to be.

## Latest in AI (newest first)
- 2026-10-21 [agent launch] Anthropic opens Claude Duet, a proactive agent that comes to you: Claude Duet sends you a morning brief from your connected apps, keeps an eye on them through the day, works on tasks while you're away, and asks before it does anything big like paying or deleting. It's a waitlist research preview for US Pro and Max subscribers, on iOS, Android and claude.ai, and Anthropic says it can still misjudge what's urgent. Source: https://claude.com/blog/claude-duet
- 2026-10-21 [industry] AI agents helped find critical PHP flaws that affect most websites: If you run a website or blog on PHP (WordPress included), make sure your host has updated PHP to the patched version now. OpenAI says its models helped researchers find the bugs before attackers did, and it's sharing a version checker and a Codex skill to help site owners check. Source: https://openai.com/index/coordinated-disclosure-of-critical-vulnerabilities
- 2026-10-21 [feature] Claude Security now re-scans your code every time it changes: Teams on Claude Enterprise can connect their code once and Claude keeps checking new changes for security holes, marking each one fixed when the fix lands. It's a public beta for businesses, not something personal plans get. Source: https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-security-now-scans-continuously-and-tracks-fixes
- 2026-10-21 [industry] OpenAI's models are coming to Google Cloud: Companies on Google Cloud will be able to use GPT-6 models and Codex without a separate OpenAI account (private preview now, wider launch planned in the coming weeks). For you it mostly means more places your work tools can quietly plug in OpenAI models. Source: https://openai.com/index/openai-models-google-cloud
- 2026-10-20 [model release] Mistral launches Voxtral 3 for voice agents that can take calls: A new set of speech models plus a kit for building phone and web voice agents that listen, look things up and talk back in 50+ languages. Mistral lists its voice agent API at $0.04 a minute with Mistral Small 4, so phone bots keep getting cheaper to run. Source: https://mistral.ai/news/voxtral-3/
- 2026-10-20 [pricing] OpenAI adds 12-hour prompt caching: Bots that run hours apart (like a morning and an evening check) can now keep their fixed instructions cached and pay the lower cached-input price. Writing to the 12-hour cache costs 2.5x the normal input price, so it pays off when the same setup is reused several times. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog
- 2026-10-20 [industry] DeepSeek open-sources the engine that runs its own API: DeepInfer is the software DeepSeek uses to serve V4.1 Flash cheaply, now free under Apache 2.0. Hosting companies can copy the tricks, which could push the price of running open models down for your bots. Source: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer
- 2026-10-18 [feature] Google turns Gemini Gems into Skills and moves Spark into the main chat: From November 17, Google starts converting personal Gems into Skills you call with a slash in the main chat, and Scheduled Actions no longer need a paid plan (still rolling out to free accounts). If you built a Gem-based bot, test it before the switch. Source: https://www.androidpolice.com/googles-renamed-gemini-features-field-guide/
- 2026-10-17 [model release] DeepSeek updates its V4.1 Flash model: faster and shorter answers, same price: DeepSeek says the update finishes tasks faster with shorter outputs, which means fewer tokens to pay for. The API name and prices are unchanged, and the open weights are on Hugging Face. Source: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/updates/
- 2026-10-17 [pricing] DeepSeek opens its own web search and page-fetch tools to developers: Bots built on DeepSeek can now search the web and read pages through DeepSeek's own API at $0.75 per 1,000 requests each. Calls made through some coding agents are free until billing starts on November 1 (Beijing time). Source: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing
- 2026-10-15 [model release] Meta releases Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weight model so far: Meta's new open model is built for coding and agent work, and you can call it on day one through Groq, OpenRouter, Together AI and other APIs. Groq runs it at 350+ tokens per second per user. That speed matters for agents, because each task is a long chain of model calls. Source: https://research.meta.ai/blog/muse-spark-open
- 2026-10-14 [model release] xAI releases Grok Voice 3.0, its new speech-to-speech model: The voice model behind Grok Bot's voice mode and Tesla's in-car assistant got an upgrade, at the same $0.08 a minute on the API. xAI says it answers in under a second and handles interruptions, which is what makes a phone bot feel natural. Source: https://x.ai/news/grok-voice-3
- 2026-10-13 [model release] Google's Gemini 4 Argon is now available to developers and paid Gemini users: Google's new top model is in the API at an introductory $2 / $10 per million tokens, and in the Gemini app for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Google built it for long, multi-step work, the kind agents do. Source: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-argon/
- 2026-10-12 [model release] Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier model: Meta says Muse Wonder will soon power its Muse personal agent, starting with paying subscribers. Developers can use it through Meta's API at $4 / $20 per million tokens. Source: https://dev.meta.ai/resources/blog/build-with-muse-wonder
- 2026-10-12 [feature] Gemini's Spark agent moves to a "Task" button on the app's home screen: Handing a job to Google's background agent is now one tap away in the Gemini app, with a new Scheduled page that shows active, paused and finished tasks. It's live on Android and iOS; web wasn't confirmed yet. Source: https://9to5google.com/2026/10/12/gemini-spark-task-redesign/

## Blueprints
- [Morning Inbox Briefing](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/morning-inbox-briefing/): Wake up to a 2-minute summary of what's in your email and what needs you today.
- [School Email Digest](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/school-email-digest-bot/): Never miss a permission slip, payment or deadline buried in school emails again.
- [Web Page Watcher](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/web-page-watcher/): Get one ping when a page you care about changes (a restock, a new listing, an appointment slot, a status update) and stop refreshing it yourself.
- [Phone Call Bot](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/phone-call-bot/): Hand off the phone calls you keep putting off: booking a table, a vet visit or a haircut, or a quick customer-service call.
- [Scam Checker](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/scam-checker/): Get a plain verdict on suspicious emails and texts before anyone in the family clicks.
- [Weekly Meal Plan Bot](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/meal-plan-bot/): Get a family meal plan and one shopping list every week without thinking about it.
- [Family Calendar Guardian](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/family-calendar-guardian/): Spot clashes and prep jobs for the next two weeks, every Sunday.
- [Travel Day Guardian](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/travel-day-guardian/): Hear about schedule changes and delays first, with your options and a request ready to send.
- [Follow-Up Finder](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/follow-up-finder/): Never let a client, lead or friend go cold because you forgot to reply.
- [Job Match Scout](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/job-match-scout/): Get a daily shortlist of jobs that fit you, with notes. You apply yourself.
- [Receipt Matcher (small business)](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/receipt-matcher/): Have every business expense matched to a receipt before your bookkeeper asks.
- [New Inquiry Logger](https://nik-schultz.github.io/agents-on-radar/blueprints/lead-logger/): Every customer inquiry lands in one tracker with a reply drafted.
